title: Ship's biscuit and hardtack
h1: Ship's biscuit and hardtack: the logic and limits of preserved starch
dek: Navies and armies fed men for months on bread baked almost to stone. The records show why it lasted when dry, how it failed when wet, and why it is not a food-storage plan for your pantry.
description: What navy records, museum objects and park pages show about ship's biscuit and Civil War hardtack, where dryness failed, and why it is not a modern storage method.
recheck: If any listed source changes, when the primary contracts cited in the Constitution Museum study are pulled and read directly, or when a modern regulator source on dry baked goods is added.

safety_review.scope: Taxonomy does not gate this item, but the page carries a food-safety verdict panel (not-validated; discard moldy bread per USDA FSIS) and no quantities, times or recipes. Requested for human read-through of the verdict panel and the decision not to link any home hardtack recipe.
